sanskrit_shloka:
कल्पार्णव इवात्यन्तपरिपूर्णैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४0१ ॥
transliteration:
kalpārṇava ivātyantaparipūrṇaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 401 ||
translation: In the One Entity which is changeless, formless and Absolute, and which is perfectly all-pervading and motionless like the ocean after the dissolution of the universe, whence can there be any diversity?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the One Entity which is changeless, formless and Absolute, and which is perfectly all-pervading and motionless like the ocean after the dissolution of the universe, whence can there be any diversity?

sanskrit_shloka:
तेजसीव तमो यत्र प्रलीनं भ्रान्तिकारणम् ।
अद्वितीये परे तत्त्वे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४0२ ॥
transliteration:
tejasīva tamo yatra pralīnaṃ bhrāntikāraṇam |
advitīye pare tattve nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 402 ||
translation: Where the root of delusion is dissolved like darkness in light – in the supreme Reality, the One without a second, the Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Where the root of delusion is dissolved like darkness in light – in the supreme Reality, the One without a second, the Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?

sanskrit_shloka:
एकात्मके परे तत्त्वे भेदवार्ता कथं वसेत् ।
सुषुप्तौ सुखमात्रायां भेदः केनावलोकितः ॥ ४0३ ॥
transliteration:
ekātmake pare tattve bhedavārtā kathaṃ vaset |
suṣuptau sukhamātrāyāṃ bhedaḥ kenāvalokitaḥ || 403 ||
translation: How can the talk of diversity apply to the Supreme Reality which is one and homogeneous? Who has ever observed diversity in the unmixed bliss of the state of profound sleep?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How can the talk of diversity apply to the Supreme Reality which is one and homogeneous? Who has ever observed diversity in the unmixed bliss of the state of profound sleep?

sanskrit_shloka:
न ह्यस्ति विश्वं परतत्त्वबोधात् सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
कालत्रये नाप्यहिरीक्षितो गुणे न ह्यम्बुबिन्दुर्मृगतृष्णिकायाम् ॥ ४0४ ॥
transliteration:
na hyasti viśvaṃ paratattvabodhāt sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
kālatraye nāpyahirīkṣito guṇe na hyambubindurmṛgatṛṣṇikāyām || 404 ||
translation: Even before the realisation of the highest Truth, the universe does not exist in the Absolute Brahman, the Essence of Existence. In none of the three states of time is the snake ever observed in the rope, nor a drop of water in the mirage.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Even before the realisation of the highest Truth, the universe does not exist in the Absolute Brahman, the Essence of Existence. In none of the three states of time is the snake ever observed in the rope, nor a drop of water in the mirage.

sanskrit_shloka:
मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः ।
इति ब्रूते श्रुतिः साक्षात्सुषुप्तावनुभूयते ॥ ४0५ ॥
transliteration:
māyāmātramidaṃ dvaitamadvaitaṃ paramārthataḥ |
iti brūte śrutiḥ sākṣātsuṣuptāvanubhūyate || 405 ||
translation: The Śrutis themselves declare that this dualistic universe is but a delusion from the standpoint of Absolute Truth. This is also experienced in the state of dreamless sleep.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Śrutis themselves declare that this dualistic universe is but a delusion from the standpoint of Absolute Truth. This is also experienced in the state of dreamless sleep.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनन्यत्वमधिष्ठानादारोप्यस्य निरीक्षितम् ।
पण्डितै रज्जुसर्पादौ विकल्पो भ्रान्तिजीवनः ॥ ४0६ ॥
transliteration:
ananyatvamadhiṣṭhānādāropyasya nirīkṣitam |
paṇḍitai rajjusarpādau vikalpo bhrāntijīvanaḥ || 406 ||
translation: That which is superimposed upon something else is observed by the wise to be identical with the substratum, as in the case of the rope appearing as the snake. The apparent difference depends solely on error.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is superimposed upon something else is observed by the wise to be identical with the substratum, as in the case of the rope appearing as the snake. The apparent difference depends solely on error.

sanskrit_shloka:
चित्तमूलो विकल्पोऽयं चित्ताभावे न कश्चन ।
अतश्चित्तं समाधेहि प्रत्यग्रूपे परात्मनि ॥ ४0७ ॥
transliteration:
cittamūlo vikalpo'yaṃ cittābhāve na kaścana |
ataścittaṃ samādhehi pratyagrūpe parātmani || 407 ||
translation: This apparent universe has its root in the mind, and never persists after the mind is annihilated. Therefore dissolve the mind by concentrating it on the Supreme Self, which is thy inmost Essence.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This apparent universe has its root in the mind, and never persists after the mind is annihilated. Therefore dissolve the mind by concentrating it on the Supreme Self, which is thy inmost Essence.

sanskrit_shloka:
किमपि सततबोधं केवलानन्दरूपं निरुपममतिवेलं नित्यमुक्तं निरीहम् ।
निरवधिगगनाभं निष्कलं निर्विकल्पं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४0८ ॥
transliteration:
kimapi satatabodhaṃ kevalānandarūpaṃ nirupamamativelaṃ nityamuktaṃ nirīham |
niravadhigaganābhaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 408 ||
translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is something of the nature of eternal Knowledge and absolute Bliss, which has no exemplar, which transcends all limitations, is ever free and without activity, and which is like the limitless sky, indivisible and absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is something of the nature of eternal Knowledge and absolute Bliss, which has no exemplar, which transcends all limitations, is ever free and without activity, and which is like the limitless sky, indivisible and absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रकृतिविकृतिशून्यं भावनातीतभावं समरसमसमानं मानसं बन्धदूरम् ।
निगमवचनसिद्धं नित्यमस्मत्प्रसिद्धं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४0९ ॥
transliteration:
prakṛtivikṛtiśūnyaṃ bhāvanātītabhāvaṃ samarasamasamānaṃ mānasaṃ bandhadūram |
nigamavacanasiddhaṃ nityamasmatprasiddhaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 409 ||
translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is devoid of the ideas of cause and effect, which is the Reality beyond all imaginations, homogeneous, matchless, beyond the range of proofs, established by the pronouncements of the Vedas, and ever familiar to us as the sense of the ego.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is devoid of the ideas of cause and effect, which is the Reality beyond all imaginations, homogeneous, matchless, beyond the range of proofs, established by the pronouncements of the Vedas, and ever familiar to us as the sense of the ego.

sanskrit_shloka:
अजरममरमस्ताभाववस्तुस्वरूपं स्तिमितसलिलराशिप्रख्यमाख्याविहीनम् ।
शमितगुणविकारं शाश्वतं शान्तमेकं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४१0 ॥
transliteration:
ajaramamaramastābhāvavastusvarūpaṃ stimitasalilarāśiprakhyamākhyāvihīnam |
śamitaguṇavikāraṃ śāśvataṃ śāntamekaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 410 ||
translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is undecaying and immortal, the positive Entity which precludes all negations, which resembles the placid ocean and is without a name, in which there are neither merits nor demerits, and which is eternal, pacified and One.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is undecaying and immortal, the positive Entity which precludes all negations, which resembles the placid ocean and is without a name, in which there are neither merits nor demerits, and which is eternal, pacified and One.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाहितान्तःकरणः स्वरूपे विलोकयात्मानमखण्डवैभवम् ।
विच्छिन्द्धि बन्धं भवगन्धगन्धितं यत्नेन पुंस्त्वं सफलीकुरुष्व ॥ ४११
transliteration:
samāhitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ svarūpe vilokayātmānamakhaṇḍavaibhavam |
vicchinddhi bandhaṃ bhavagandhagandhitaṃ yatnena puṃstvaṃ saphalīkuruṣva || 411
translation: With the mind restrained in Samadhi, behold in thy self the Ātman, of infinite glory, cut off thy bondage strengthened by the impressions of previous births, and carefully attain the consummation of thy birth as a human being.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: With the mind restrained in Samadhi, behold in thy self the Ātman, of infinite glory, cut off thy bondage strengthened by the impressions of previous births, and carefully attain the consummation of thy birth as a human being.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तं सच्चिदानन्दमद्वयम् ।
भावयात्मानमात्मस्थं न भूयः कल्पसेऽध्वने ॥ ४१२ ॥
transliteration:
sarvopādhivinirmuktaṃ saccidānandamadvayam |
bhāvayātmānamātmasthaṃ na bhūyaḥ kalpase'dhvane || 412 ||
translation: Meditate on the Ātman, which resides in thee, which is devoid of all limiting adjuncts, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thou shalt no more come under the round of births and deaths.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Meditate on the Ātman, which resides in thee, which is devoid of all limiting adjuncts, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thou shalt no more come under the round of births and deaths.

sanskrit_shloka:
छायेव पुंसः परिदृश्यमान् माभासरूपेण फलानुभूत्या ।
शरीरमाराच्छववन्निरस्तं पुनर्न संधत्त इदं महात्मा ॥ ४१३ ॥
transliteration:
chāyeva puṃsaḥ paridṛśyamān mābhāsarūpeṇa phalānubhūtyā |
śarīramārācchavavannirastaṃ punarna saṃdhatta idaṃ mahātmā || 413 ||
translation: After the body has once been cast off to a distance like a corpse, the sage never more attaches himself to it, though it is visible as an appearance, like the shadow of a man, owing to the experience of the effects of past deeds.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: After the body has once been cast off to a distance like a corpse, the sage never more attaches himself to it, though it is visible as an appearance, like the shadow of a man, owing to the experience of the effects of past deeds.

sanskrit_shloka:
सततविमलबोधानन्दरूपं समेत्य त्यज जडमलरूपोपाधिमेतं सुदूरे ।
अथ पुनरपि नैष स्मर्यतां वान्तवस्तु स्मरणविषयभूतं पल्पते कुत्सनाय ॥ ४१४ ॥
transliteration:
satatavimalabodhānandarūpaṃ sametya tyaja jaḍamalarūpopādhimetaṃ sudūre |
atha punarapi naiṣa smaryatāṃ vāntavastu smaraṇaviṣayabhūtaṃ palpate kutsanāya || 414 ||
translation: Realising the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss, throw far away this limitation of a body, which is inert and filthy by nature. Then remember it no more, for something that has been vomited excites but disgust when called in memory.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss, throw far away this limitation of a body, which is inert and filthy by nature. Then remember it no more, for something that has been vomited excites but disgust when called in memory.

sanskrit_shloka:
समूलमेतत्परिदाह्य वन्हौ सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
ततः स्वयं नित्यविशुद्धबोधा नन्दात्मना तिष्ठति विद्वरिष्ठः ॥ ४१५ ॥
transliteration:
samūlametatparidāhya vanhau sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
tataḥ svayaṃ nityaviśuddhabodhā nandātmanā tiṣṭhati vidvariṣṭhaḥ || 415 ||
translation: Burning all this, with its very root, in the fire of Brahman, the Eternal and Absolute Self, the truly wise man thereafter remains alone, as the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Burning all this, with its very root, in the fire of Brahman, the Eternal and Absolute Self, the truly wise man thereafter remains alone, as the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रारब्धसूत्रग्रथितं शरीरं प्रयातु वा तिष्ठतु गोरिव स्रक् ।
न तत्पुनः पश्यति तत्त्ववेत्ता (आ)नन्दात्मनि ब्रह्मणि लीनवृत्तिः ॥ ४१६ ॥
transliteration:
prārabdhasūtragrathitaṃ śarīraṃ prayātu vā tiṣṭhatu goriva srak |
na tatpunaḥ paśyati tattvavettā (ā)nandātmani brahmaṇi līnavṛttiḥ || 416 ||
translation: The knower of Truth does no more care whether this body, spun out by the threads of Prārabdha work, falls or remains – like the garland on a cow – for his mind-functions are at rest in the Brahman, the Essence of Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The knower of Truth does no more care whether this body, spun out by the threads of Prārabdha work, falls or remains – like the garland on a cow – for his mind-functions are at rest in the Brahman, the Essence of Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
अखण्डानन्दमात्मानं विज्ञाय स्वस्वरूपतः ।
किमिच्छन् कस्य वा हेतोर्देहं पुष्णाति तत्त्ववित् ॥ ४१७ ॥
transliteration:
akhaṇḍānandamātmānaṃ vijñāya svasvarūpataḥ |
kimicchan kasya vā hetordehaṃ puṣṇāti tattvavit || 417 ||
translation: Realising the Ātman, the Infinite Bliss, as his very Self, with what object, or for whom, should the knower of Truth cherish the body.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising the Ātman, the Infinite Bliss, as his very Self, with what object, or for whom, should the knower of Truth cherish the body.

sanskrit_shloka:
संसिद्धस्य फलं त्वेतज्जीवन्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ।
बहिरन्तः सदानन्दरसास्वादनमात्मनि ॥ ४१८ ॥
transliteration:
saṃsiddhasya phalaṃ tvetajjīvanmuktasya yoginaḥ |
bahirantaḥ sadānandarasāsvādanamātmani || 418 ||
translation: The Yogi who has attained perfection and is liberated-in-life gets this as result – he enjoys eternal Bliss in his mind, internally as well as externally.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Yogi who has attained perfection and is liberated-in-life gets this as result – he enjoys eternal Bliss in his mind, internally as well as externally.

sanskrit_shloka:
वैराग्यस्य फलं बोधो बोधस्योपरतिः फलम् ।
स्वानन्दानुभवाच्छान्तिरेषैवोपरतेः फलम् ॥ ४१९ ॥
transliteration:
vairāgyasya phalaṃ bodho bodhasyoparatiḥ phalam |
svānandānubhavācchāntireṣaivoparateḥ phalam || 419 ||
translation: The result of dispassion is knowledge, that of Knowledge is withdrawal from sense-pleasures, which leads to the experience of the Bliss of the Self, whence follows Peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The result of dispassion is knowledge, that of Knowledge is withdrawal from sense-pleasures, which leads to the experience of the Bliss of the Self, whence follows Peace.

sanskrit_shloka:
यद्युत्तरोत्तराभावः पूर्वपूर्वन्तु निष्फलम् ।
निवृत्तिः परमा तृप्तिरानन्दोऽनुपमः स्वतः ॥ ४२0 ॥
transliteration:
yadyuttarottarābhāvaḥ pūrvapūrvantu niṣphalam |
nivṛttiḥ paramā tṛptirānando'nupamaḥ svataḥ || 420 ||
translation: If there is an absence of the succeeding stages, the preceding ones are futile. (When the series is perfect) the cessation of the objective world, extreme satisfaction, and matchless bliss follow as a matter of course.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If there is an absence of the succeeding stages, the preceding ones are futile. (When the series is perfect) the cessation of the objective world, extreme satisfaction, and matchless bliss follow as a matter of course.

sanskrit_shloka:
दृष्टदुःखेष्वनुद्वेगो विद्यायाः प्रस्तुतं फलम् ।
यत्कृतं भ्रान्तिवेलायां नाना कर्म जुगुप्सितम् पश्चान्नरो विवेकेन तत्कथं कर्तुमर्हति ॥ ४२१ ॥
transliteration:
dṛṣṭaduḥkheṣvanudvego vidyāyāḥ prastutaṃ phalam |
yatkṛtaṃ bhrāntivelāyāṃ nānā karma jugupsitam paścānnaro vivekena tatkathaṃ kartumarhati || 421 ||
translation: Being unruffled by earthly troubles is the result in question of knowledge. How can a man who did various loathsome deeds during the state of delusion, commit the same afterwards, possessed of discrimination?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Being unruffled by earthly troubles is the result in question of knowledge. How can a man who did various loathsome deeds during the state of delusion, commit the same afterwards, possessed of discrimination?

sanskrit_shloka:
विद्याफलं स्यादसतो निवृत्तिः प्रवृत्तिरज्ञानफलं तदीक्षितम् ।
तज्ज्ञाज्ञयोर्यन्मृगतृष्णिकादौ नोचेद्विदां दृष्टफलं किमस्मात् ॥ ४२२ ॥
transliteration:
vidyāphalaṃ syādasato nivṛttiḥ pravṛttirajñānaphalaṃ tadīkṣitam |
tajjñājñayoryanmṛgatṛṣṇikādau nocedvidāṃ dṛṣṭaphalaṃ kimasmāt || 422 ||
translation: The result of knowledge should be the turning away from unreal things, while attachment to these is the result of ignorance. This is observed in the case of one who knows a mirage and things of that sort, and one who does not. Otherwise, what other tangible result do the knowers of Brahman obtain?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The result of knowledge should be the turning away from unreal things, while attachment to these is the result of ignorance. This is observed in the case of one who knows a mirage and things of that sort, and one who does not. Otherwise, what other tangible result do the knowers of Brahman obtain?

sanskrit_shloka:
अज्ञानहृदयग्रन्थेर्विनाशो यद्यशेषतः ।
अनिच्छोर्विषयः किं नु प्रवृत्तेः कारणं स्वतः ॥ ४२३ ॥
transliteration:
ajñānahṛdayagranthervināśo yadyaśeṣataḥ |
anicchorviṣayaḥ kiṃ nu pravṛtteḥ kāraṇaṃ svataḥ || 423 ||
translation: If the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed, what natural cause can there be for inducing such a man to selfish action, for he is averse to sense-pleasures?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed, what natural cause can there be for inducing such a man to selfish action, for he is averse to sense-pleasures?

sanskrit_shloka:
वासनानुदयो भोग्ये वैरागस्य तदावधिः ।
अहंभावोदयाभावो बोधस्य परमावधिः लीनवृत्तैरनुत्पत्तिर्मर्यादोपरतेस्तु सा ॥ ४२४ ॥
transliteration:
vāsanānudayo bhogye vairāgasya tadāvadhiḥ |
ahaṃbhāvodayābhāvo bodhasya paramāvadhiḥ līnavṛttairanutpattirmaryādoparatestu sā || 424 ||
translation: When the sense-objects excite no more desire, then is the culmination of dispassion. The extreme perfection of knowledge is the absence of any impulsion of the egoistic idea. And the limit of self-withdrawal is reached when the mind-functions that have been merged, appear no more.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the sense-objects excite no more desire, then is the culmination of dispassion. The extreme perfection of knowledge is the absence of any impulsion of the egoistic idea. And the limit of self-withdrawal is reached when the mind-functions that have been merged, appear no more.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्माकारतया सदा स्थिततया निर्मुक्तबाह्यार्थधीर् अन्यावेदितभोग्यभोगकलनो निद्रालुवद्बालवत् ।
स्वप्नालोकितलोकवज्जगदिदं पश्यन् क्वचिल्लब्धधीर् आस्ते कश्चिदनन्तपुण्यफलभुग्धन्यः स मान्यो भुवि ॥ ४२५ ॥
transliteration:
brahmākāratayā sadā sthitatayā nirmuktabāhyārthadhīr anyāveditabhogyabhogakalano nidrāluvadbālavat |
svapnālokitalokavajjagadidaṃ paśyan kvacillabdhadhīr āste kaścidanantapuṇyaphalabhugdhanyaḥ sa mānyo bhuvi || 425 ||
translation: Freed from all sense of reality of the external sense-objects on account of his always remaining merged in Brahman; only seeming to enjoy such sense-objects as are offered by others, like one sleepy, or like a child; beholding this world as one seen in dreams, and having cognition of it at chance moments – rare indeed is such a man, the enjoyer of the fruits of endless merit, and he alone is blessed and esteemed on earth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Freed from all sense of reality of the external sense-objects on account of his always remaining merged in Brahman; only seeming to enjoy such sense-objects as are offered by others, like one sleepy, or like a child; beholding this world as one seen in dreams, and having cognition of it at chance moments – rare indeed is such a man, the enjoyer of the fruits of endless merit, and he alone is blessed and esteemed on earth.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्थितप्रज्ञो यतिरयं यः सदानन्दमश्नुते ।
ब्रह्मण्येव विलीनात्मा निर्विकारो विनिष्क्रियः ॥ ४२६ ॥
transliteration:
sthitaprajño yatirayaṃ yaḥ sadānandamaśnute |
brahmaṇyeva vilīnātmā nirvikāro viniṣkriyaḥ || 426 ||
translation: That Sannyasin has got a steady illumination who, having his soul wholly merged in Brahman, enjoys eternal bliss, is changeless and free from activity.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That Sannyasin has got a steady illumination who, having his soul wholly merged in Brahman, enjoys eternal bliss, is changeless and free from activity.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मात्मनोः शोधितयोरेकभावावगाहिनी ।
निर्विकल्पा च चिन्मात्रा वृत्तिः प्रज्ञेति कथ्यते सुस्थितासौ भवेद्यस्य स्थितप्रज्ञः स उच्यते ॥ ४२७ ॥
transliteration:
brahmātmanoḥ śodhitayorekabhāvāvagāhinī |
nirvikalpā ca cinmātrā vṛttiḥ prajñeti kathyate susthitāsau bhavedyasya sthitaprajñaḥ sa ucyate || 427 ||
translation: That kind of mental function which cognises only the identity of the Self and Brahman, purified of all adjuncts, which is free from duality, and which concerns itself only with Pure Intelligence, is called illumination. He who has this perfectly steady is called a man of steady illumination.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That kind of mental function which cognises only the identity of the Self and Brahman, purified of all adjuncts, which is free from duality, and which concerns itself only with Pure Intelligence, is called illumination. He who has this perfectly steady is called a man of steady illumination.

sanskrit_shloka:
यस्य स्थिता भवेत्प्रज्ञा यस्यानन्दो निरन्तरः ।
प्रपञ्चो विस्मृतप्रायः स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४२८ ॥
transliteration:
yasya sthitā bhavetprajñā yasyānando nirantaraḥ |
prapañco vismṛtaprāyaḥ sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 428 ||
translation: He whose illumination is steady, who has constant bliss, and who has almost forgotten the phenomenal universe, is accepted as a man liberated in this very life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He whose illumination is steady, who has constant bliss, and who has almost forgotten the phenomenal universe, is accepted as a man liberated in this very life.

sanskrit_shloka:
लीनधीरपि जागर्ति जाग्रद्धर्मविवर्जितः ।
बोधो निर्वासनो यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४२९ ॥
transliteration:
līnadhīrapi jāgarti jāgraddharmavivarjitaḥ |
bodho nirvāsano yasya sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 429 ||
translation: He who, even having his mind merged in Brahman, is nevertheless quite alert, but free at the same time from the characteristics of the waking state, and whose realisation is free from desires, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who, even having his mind merged in Brahman, is nevertheless quite alert, but free at the same time from the characteristics of the waking state, and whose realisation is free from desires, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
शान्तसंसारकलनः कलावानपि निष्कलः ।
यस्य चित्तं विनिश्चिन्तं स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४३0 ॥
transliteration:
śāntasaṃsārakalanaḥ kalāvānapi niṣkalaḥ |
yasya cittaṃ viniścintaṃ sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 430 ||
translation: He whose cares about the phenomenal state have been appeased, who, though possessed of a body consisting of parts, is yet devoid of parts, and whose mind is free from anxiety, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He whose cares about the phenomenal state have been appeased, who, though possessed of a body consisting of parts, is yet devoid of parts, and whose mind is free from anxiety, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
वर्तमानेऽपि देहेऽस्मिञ्छायावदनुवर्तिनि ।
अहन्ताममताभावो जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३१ ॥
transliteration:
vartamāne'pi dehe'smiñchāyāvadanuvartini |
ahantāmamatābhāvo jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 431 ||
translation: The absence of the ideas of 'I' and 'mine' even in this existing body which follows as a shadow, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The absence of the ideas of 'I' and 'mine' even in this existing body which follows as a shadow, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतीताननुसन्धानं भविष्यदविचारणम् ।
अउदासीन्यमपि प्राप्तं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३२ ॥
transliteration:
atītānanusandhānaṃ bhaviṣyadavicāraṇam |
audāsīnyamapi prāptaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 432 ||
translation: Not dwelling on enjoyments of the past, taking no thought for the future and looking with indifference upon the present, are characteristics of one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Not dwelling on enjoyments of the past, taking no thought for the future and looking with indifference upon the present, are characteristics of one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
गुणदोषविशिष्टेऽस्मिन्स्वभावेन विलक्षणे ।
सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३३ ॥
transliteration:
guṇadoṣaviśiṣṭe'sminsvabhāvena vilakṣaṇe |
sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 433 ||
translation: Looking everywhere with an eye of equality in this world, full of elements possessing merits and demerits, and distinct by nature from one another, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Looking everywhere with an eye of equality in this world, full of elements possessing merits and demerits, and distinct by nature from one another, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
इष्टानिष्टार्थसम्प्राप्तौ समदर्शितयात्मनि ।
उभयत्राविकारित्वं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३४ ॥
transliteration:
iṣṭāniṣṭārthasamprāptau samadarśitayātmani |
ubhayatrāvikāritvaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 434 ||
translation: When things pleasant or painful present themselves, to remain unruffled in mind in both cases, through the sameness of attitude, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When things pleasant or painful present themselves, to remain unruffled in mind in both cases, through the sameness of attitude, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मानन्दरसास्वादासक्तचित्ततया यतेः ।
अन्तर्बहिरविज्ञानं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३५ ॥
transliteration:
brahmānandarasāsvādāsaktacittatayā yateḥ |
antarbahiravijñānaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 435 ||
translation: The absence of all ideas of interior or exterior in the case of a Sannyasin, owing to his mind being engrossed in tasting the bliss of Brahman, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The absence of all ideas of interior or exterior in the case of a Sannyasin, owing to his mind being engrossed in tasting the bliss of Brahman, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहेन्द्रियादौ कर्तव्ये ममाहंभाववर्जितः ।
अउदासीन्येन यस्तिष्ठेत्स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३६ ॥
transliteration:
dehendriyādau kartavye mamāhaṃbhāvavarjitaḥ |
audāsīnyena yastiṣṭhetsa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 436 ||
translation: He who lives unconcerned, devoid of all ideas of 'I' and 'mine' with regard to the body, organs, etc., as well as to his duties, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who lives unconcerned, devoid of all ideas of 'I' and 'mine' with regard to the body, organs, etc., as well as to his duties, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
विज्ञात आत्मनो यस्य ब्रह्मभावः श्रुतेर्बलात् ।
भवबन्धविनिर्मुक्तः स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३७ ॥
transliteration:
vijñāta ātmano yasya brahmabhāvaḥ śruterbalāt |
bhavabandhavinirmuktaḥ sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 437 ||
translation: He who has realised his Brahmanhood aided by the Scriptures, and is free from the bondage of transmigration, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who has realised his Brahmanhood aided by the Scriptures, and is free from the bondage of transmigration, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहेन्द्रियेष्वहंभाव इदंभावस्तदन्यके ।
यस्य नो भवतः क्वापि स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४३८ ॥
transliteration:
dehendriyeṣvahaṃbhāva idaṃbhāvastadanyake |
yasya no bhavataḥ kvāpi sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 438 ||
translation: He who never has the idea of 'I' with regard to the body, organs, etc., nor that of 'it' in respect of things other than these, is accepted as one liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who never has the idea of 'I' with regard to the body, organs, etc., nor that of 'it' in respect of things other than these, is accepted as one liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
न प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मणोर्भेदं कदापि ब्रह्मसर्गयोः ।
प्रज्ञया यो विजानिति स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३९ ॥
transliteration:
na pratyagbrahmaṇorbhedaṃ kadāpi brahmasargayoḥ |
prajñayā yo vijāniti sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 439 ||
translation: He who through his illumination never differentiates the Jiva and Brahman, nor the universe and Brahman, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who through his illumination never differentiates the Jiva and Brahman, nor the universe and Brahman, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
साधुभिः पूज्यमानेऽस्मिन् पीड्यमानेऽपि दुर्जनैः ।
समभावो भवेद्यस्य स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४४0 ॥
transliteration:
sādhubhiḥ pūjyamāne'smin pīḍyamāne'pi durjanaiḥ |
samabhāvo bhavedyasya sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 440 ||
translation: He who feels just the same when his body is either worshipped by the good or tormented by the wicked, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who feels just the same when his body is either worshipped by the good or tormented by the wicked, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्र प्रविष्टा विषयाः परेरिता नदीप्रवाहा इव वारिराशौ ।
लिनन्ति सन्मात्रतया न विक्रियां उत्पादयन्त्येष यतिर्विमुक्तः ॥ ४४१ ॥
transliteration:
yatra praviṣṭā viṣayāḥ pareritā nadīpravāhā iva vārirāśau |
linanti sanmātratayā na vikriyāṃ utpādayantyeṣa yatirvimuktaḥ || 441 ||
translation: The Sannyasin in whom the sense-objects directed by others are engulfed like flowing rivers in the sea and produce no change, owing to his identity with the Existence Absolute, is indeed liberated.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Sannyasin in whom the sense-objects directed by others are engulfed like flowing rivers in the sea and produce no change, owing to his identity with the Existence Absolute, is indeed liberated.

sanskrit_shloka:
विज्ञातब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य यथापूर्वं न संसृतिः ।
अस्ति चेन्न स विज्ञातब्रह्मभावो बहिर्मुखः ॥ ४४२ ॥
transliteration:
vijñātabrahmatattvasya yathāpūrvaṃ na saṃsṛtiḥ |
asti cenna sa vijñātabrahmabhāvo bahirmukhaḥ || 442 ||
translation: For one who has realised the Truth of Brahman, there is no more attachment to the sense-objects as before: If there is, that man has not realised his identity with Brahman, but is one whose senses are outgoing in their tendency.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For one who has realised the Truth of Brahman, there is no more attachment to the sense-objects as before: If there is, that man has not realised his identity with Brahman, but is one whose senses are outgoing in their tendency.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्राचीनवासनावेगादसौ संसरतीति चेत् ।
न सदेकत्वविज्ञानान्मन्दी भवति वासना ॥ ४४३ ॥
transliteration:
prācīnavāsanāvegādasau saṃsaratīti cet |
na sadekatvavijñānānmandī bhavati vāsanā || 443 ||
translation: If it be urged that he is still attached to the sense-objects through the momentum of his old desires, the reply is – no, for desires get weakened through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If it be urged that he is still attached to the sense-objects through the momentum of his old desires, the reply is – no, for desires get weakened through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
अत्यन्तकामुकस्यापि वृत्तिः कुण्ठति मातरि ।
तथैव ब्रह्मणि ज्ञाते पूर्णानन्दे मनीषिणः ॥ ४४४ ॥
transliteration:
atyantakāmukasyāpi vṛttiḥ kuṇṭhati mātari |
tathaiva brahmaṇi jñāte pūrṇānande manīṣiṇaḥ || 444 ||
translation: The propensities of even a confirmed libertine are checked in the presence of his mother; just so, when Brahman, the Bliss Absolute, has been realised, the man of realisation has no longer any worldly tendency.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The propensities of even a confirmed libertine are checked in the presence of his mother; just so, when Brahman, the Bliss Absolute, has been realised, the man of realisation has no longer any worldly tendency.

sanskrit_shloka:
निदिध्यासनशीलस्य बाह्यप्रत्यय ईक्ष्यते ।
ब्रवीति श्रुतिरेतस्य प्रारब्धं फलदर्शनात् ॥ ४४५ ॥
transliteration:
nididhyāsanaśīlasya bāhyapratyaya īkṣyate |
bravīti śrutiretasya prārabdhaṃ phaladarśanāt || 445 ||
translation: One who is constantly practising meditation is observed to have external perceptions. The Śrutis mention Prārabdha work in the case of such a man, and we can infer this from results actually seen.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: One who is constantly practising meditation is observed to have external perceptions. The Śrutis mention Prārabdha work in the case of such a man, and we can infer this from results actually seen.

sanskrit_shloka:
सुखाद्यनुभवो यावत्तावत्प्रारब्धमिष्यते ।
फलोदयः क्रियापूर्वो निष्क्रियो न हि कुत्रचित् ॥ ४४६ ॥
transliteration:
sukhādyanubhavo yāvattāvatprārabdhamiṣyate |
phalodayaḥ kriyāpūrvo niṣkriyo na hi kutracit || 446 ||
translation: Prārabdha work is acknowledged to persist so long as there is the perception of happiness and the like. Every result is preceded by an action, and nowhere is it seen to accrue independently of action.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Prārabdha work is acknowledged to persist so long as there is the perception of happiness and the like. Every result is preceded by an action, and nowhere is it seen to accrue independently of action.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानात्कल्पकोटिशतार्जितम् ।
सञ्चितं विलयं याति प्रबोधात्स्वप्नकर्मवत् ॥ ४४७ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ brahmeti vijñānātkalpakoṭiśatārjitam |
sañcitaṃ vilayaṃ yāti prabodhātsvapnakarmavat || 447 ||
translation: Through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman, all the accumulated actions of a hundred crore of cycles come to nought, like the actions of dream-state on awakening.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman, all the accumulated actions of a hundred crore of cycles come to nought, like the actions of dream-state on awakening.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्कृतं स्वप्नवेलायां पुण्यं वा पापमुल्बणम् ।
सुप्तोत्थितस्य किं तत्स्यात्स्वर्गाय नरकाय वा ॥ ४४८ ॥
transliteration:
yatkṛtaṃ svapnavelāyāṃ puṇyaṃ vā pāpamulbaṇam |
suptotthitasya kiṃ tatsyātsvargāya narakāya vā || 448 ||
translation: Can the good actions or dreadful sins that a man fancies himself doing in the dream-state, lead him to heaven or hell after he has awakened from sleep?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Can the good actions or dreadful sins that a man fancies himself doing in the dream-state, lead him to heaven or hell after he has awakened from sleep?

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वमसङ्गमुदासीनं परिज्ञाय नभो यथा ।
न श्लिष्यति च यत्किंचित्कदाचिद्भाविकर्मभिः ॥ ४४९ ॥
transliteration:
svamasaṅgamudāsīnaṃ parijñāya nabho yathā |
na śliṣyati ca yatkiṃcitkadācidbhāvikarmabhiḥ || 449 ||
translation: Realising the Ātman, which is unattached and indifferent like the sky, the aspirant is never touched in the least by actions yet to be done.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising the Ātman, which is unattached and indifferent like the sky, the aspirant is never touched in the least by actions yet to be done.

sanskrit_shloka:
न नभो घटयोगेन सुरागन्धेन लिप्यते ।
तथात्मोपाधियोगेन तद्धर्मैर्नैव लिप्यते ॥ ४५0 ॥
transliteration:
na nabho ghaṭayogena surāgandhena lipyate |
tathātmopādhiyogena taddharmairnaiva lipyate || 450 ||
translation: The sky is not affected by the smell of liquor merely through its connection with the jar; similarly, the Ātman is not, through Its connection with the limitations, affected by the properties thereof.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sky is not affected by the smell of liquor merely through its connection with the jar; similarly, the Ātman is not, through Its connection with the limitations, affected by the properties thereof.
